record.paper_title: Known results and open problems in hypercomplex convexity
record.original_question: What is the minimal number of pairwise disjoint balls, each centered on the sphere S^{n−1}, needed so that every straight line passing through the center of the sphere intersects at least one of those balls?

evidence.quote:
Problem 7. (The shadow problem ). What is minimal number of
pair wise disjoint balls with the centre on sphere Sn−1 it is enough that any
straight line, getting through the centre of the sphere, crossed at least one of
those balls?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $S^{n-1} = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \|x\| = 1\}$ denote the unit sphere in $n$-dimensional Euclidean space, centered at the origin $O$. Consider finite families $\mathcal{F} = \{B_1, \dots, B_N\}$ of pairwise disjoint closed Euclidean balls $B_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ such that the center of each $B_i$ lies on $S^{n-1}$ and $O \notin B_i$ for all $i$. Say that $\mathcal{F}$ "creates a shadow at $O$" if every straight line in $\mathbb{R}^n$ passing through $O$ intersects at least one ball $B_i$. Determine, for each $n \geq 2$, the minimum cardinality $N(n)$ of such a family $\mathcal{F}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The planar case $n=2$ is known to have minimum number 3. In general dimension $n$, it is known that $n+1$ pairwise disjoint balls suffice, and various partial results and generalizations (e.g., to ellipsoids, fixed-radius balls, complex case) have been studied, but the exact minimum $N(n)$ for $n \geq 3$ does not appear to be settled in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On the shadow problem and its generalizations to ellipsoids
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the shadow problem and generalizations to ellipsoids.
status_evidence.claim: The shadow problem and its generalizations remain an active area, with sufficiency results (n+1 balls suffice) but no general sharp minimum known.

status_evidence.title: Problem of shadow (complex case)
status_evidence.snippet: For n=2 the minimal number equals three; n+1 balls suffice in R^n.
status_evidence.claim: Planar case solved (=3); higher-dimensional exact minimum not established.

status_evidence.title: The problem of shadow for balls with fixed radius
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates fixed-radius variants of the shadow problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related variants studied, indicating the general problem is not fully resolved.
